#1977. Why Pochettino’s pressing style could suit Man Utd and what stands in the way

By Alexis Pereira | 10 Nov 2026 18:12

Manchester United face another decision that could define their season. After a disastrous start to the Premier League, with the team in the relegation zone and winless in eight games, Michael Carrick has lost support inside the club. The hierarchy is weighing a change at the top, and according to the English press, Mauricio Pochettino is the leading candidate to take over.

The possibility carries both opportunity and urgency. The Argentinian manager is in charge of the United States national team, but he has a contract clause that would allow him to leave in return for financial compensation. He also knows the Premier League deeply and has come close to taking the United job on other occasions. At 54, he combines experience at high-pressure clubs, rebuilding projects and a style of play that could, in theory, give the Red Devils a clearer identity. That does not mean he is an automatic solution.

Carrick’s situation has deteriorated quickly. After a vote of confidence from the hierarchy, he was given three more games to change the picture. The result was not enough, as United won only once in that period and reached eight games without a Premier League victory. The 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on Sunday kept the team in the relegation zone and increased the pressure for a decision.

On Tuesday, the situation was not officially settled. Sky Sports reported that the hierarchy was carrying out a full performance review, led by director of football Jason Wilcox, and intended to decide Carrick’s future before the end of the international break. ESPN named Pochettino as the board’s preferred candidate if a dismissal goes ahead.

The Argentinian is not new to the club. He has been interviewed for the job on three previous occasions and was among the top names considered in selection processes that ended with other appointments. In an interview with FourFourTwo in May, Pochettino acknowledged that United had shown repeated interest but said the ideal opportunity never materialised.

There is, however, an important contractual question. In August, after the World Cup, Pochettino signed a renewal with the United States Soccer Federation that extends his deal to 2030. According to The Athletic, there is an exit clause of around $10m (about £7.5m). The mechanism would allow an interested club to trigger the clause by paying the compensation. The figure would not necessarily cover the whole coaching staff, however. Pochettino has worked for many years with trusted staff such as assistant Jesus Perez, and releasing those members could push up the cost.

It is also important to understand the scale of the commitment he made to the United States. The renewal was not simply an extension to lead the team at the next World Cup: the federation announced that Pochettino and his team would have a wider role in developing the sport in the country, including youth categories, coach education and technical structure.

Tactically, there are reasons why the name appeals to United. Pochettino built his reputation in England at Southampton and Tottenham Hotspur, teams that combined high pressing, intensity without the ball and vertical attacks. At Tottenham in particular, he turned a young squad into a competitive team that challenged for domestic honours and reached the 2019 Champions League final.

His model usually starts from a 4-2-3-1 or a 4-3-3. In build-up, the centre-backs split, the holding midfielders offer passing lines and the full-backs advance to provide width. The aim is to create numerical superiority in certain areas, draw the opposition press and find space to progress. In attack, the wingers can leave the touchline and occupy inside channels, while the full-backs provide depth on the outside.

The most recognisable feature is the way he defends. Pochettino likes aggressive teams that press the opposition build-up and try to win the ball back quickly after losing it. For that, he needs players able to repeat efforts, close space and keep distances between the lines.

That principle could be interesting for United, who have struggled to find a consistent identity. The Red Devils have more possession, but do not necessarily turn that control into dominance. They have also shown problems sustaining a high block: when the first press is beaten, a lack of mobility and coordination between midfield and defence opens space for the opposition.

Pochettino could offer an answer. Instead of relying on individual moments of pressing, United would have a more defined model to guide the movement of the attackers, the cover of the midfielders and the positioning of the defensive line. There is a condition, however: the squad must be compatible with the manager’s physical demands. He does not usually compromise on commitment without the ball and has shown, in different jobs, a willingness to sideline players who cannot keep up with the intensity he wants. United have players with suitable characteristics, but also imbalances in important areas.

Pochettino has a track record that could help with another aspect of the crisis: squad management. At Tottenham, he worked with a squad that mixed experienced players and rising youngsters, developing names such as Harry Kane and Dele Alli. He also valued homegrown players and built an environment of collective demand. At Southampton, he helped consolidate a competitive team with players who were still establishing themselves.

That ability to develop young players fits one of United’s historic characteristics. The club has a tradition of backing academy talent, but needs to turn that principle into a coherent sporting policy and not just an occasional solution for difficult moments.

His profile also involves demands for intensity and discipline. He is not a manager known for building relationships around names or status. Even so, calling this a guarantee that he will impose order at Old Trafford would oversimplify the problem. A manager’s firm hand only produces lasting effects when there is backing from the hierarchy and a structure that supports his decisions.

That is where the biggest doubt lies over a possible appointment. United have gone through successive changes of manager, sporting project and transfer strategy. The current crisis did not arise only from Carrick’s tactical choices: the squad has imbalances, the board has to set priorities and the club is still searching for stability in how football is run.

Pochettino’s experience at Chelsea also recommends caution. In London, he improved the team’s performance and finished sixth in the 2023-24 Premier League, but did not stay in the job to continue the project. In Paris, he won the French league title with Paris Saint-Germain, but struggled to balance a squad full of stars and meet the club’s European expectations.

United need a manager who can stabilise the team in the short term and at the same time set a direction for the future. Pochettino has Premier League experience, knows the pressure of running a club with a huge fanbase and offers a playing proposal that could give the team an identity. It is not a baseless bet. He could be a sporting solution that makes sense. What is still unclear is whether United are ready to provide the conditions he needs to succeed.

#1976. Scotland team to play North Macedonia: where McTominay fits in, new-look defence, striker decision

Predicted Scotland XI for Nations League clash at Hampden on Friday

Sebastien Pocognoli will bid for his first Hampden victory at the third attempt when Scotland host North Macedonia on Friday.

The Scotland head coach endured an underwhelming start to his tenure last month by picking up just four points from a possible 12 in the Nations League while losing both of his home openers against Switzerland and Slovenia.

The away performances at least provided some encourgament with a strong second half in the goalless draw against Slovenia in Ljubljana in his first match in charge and a dominant 2-0 win over North Macedonia in Skopje.

However, the 2-1 defeat by Slovenia at Hampden ended his maiden camp on a sour note and raised questions over whether the squad is suited to the manager's preferred system, with Pocognoli using a 3-4-2-1 or 3-4-1-2 formation across his first four games.

The squad has been bolstered by the return of Scott McTominay, Kieran Tierney and Che Adams but defenders Stephen Welsh and Luis Binks have withdrawn and replaced by Ryan Porteous and David Bates, while Scott McKenna is also absent.

Assuming Pocognoli sticks with his preferred set-up, here is our preferred starting XI for the game against North Macedonia at Hampden on Friday, with an away trip to Switzerland to follow on Monday.

The San Jose Earthquakes goalkeeper was the first choice pick for Steve Clarke towards the end of his tenure, and has retained the gloves under Pocognoli thus far, starting all four matches last month. #1975. Home wobbles are a puzzle for Horsham FC boss after AFC Totton defeat

The Hornets saw their five-match unbeaten run in National League South come to an end at home to the Stags, Saturday’s game finishing 3-2 to the visitors.

Horsham have won just twice at home in the league in 2026-27, recording eight points in as many games.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

That is in stark contrast to the Hornets’ away form. They have taken 14 points from eight games and have yet to be beaten on the road.

And their home performances in the league have confounded Di Paola.

He told us: “It’s annoying. There’s been a few at home where you’re scratching your head as to why you’ve not got anything out of them.

“Maidstone we should have got more out of, Farnham we should have got more out of, Totton we should have got more out of. There’s been lots of opportunities for us to do better at home – and we have to do better at home.

“It’s hard to put your finger on why because we’re quite dominant in these games. I hate stats but we had 60 per cent possession on Saturday, double the amount of shots, double everything really – but it doesn’t mean anything.

“At home there seems to be a common thread where we dominate games but don’t capitalise – yet when we go away we’re perhaps not as dominant but we pick up points.

“Maybe we need to have a reset in how we approach home games because it’s clearly not working.

“But if you look at every metric apart from points and wins, we’re doing really well so there’s something fundamentally wrong.”

Totton led twice in the first half only for the Hornets to strike back both times through Charlie Hester-Cook and Ryan Bartley.

Josh Sims hit what proved to be the Stags’ winner on 72 minutes to bring Horsham’s unbeaten streak to an end.

Defeat to Totton saw the Hornets drop two places to 12th.

Di Paola added: “They had three shots on target and scored all three. We just don’t capitalise when we’re on top. We don’t seem to be able to pull away from teams.

“We got back to 1-1 and then we gave away a really poor goal from a corner. We got it back to 2-2 and we’re on the march, but they’ve gone down the other end and scored and it’s almost game over.

“We were chasing it but they were able to park the bus and they just sat in and made it really hard for us to score – like we’ve done to teams.

“On Saturday – and you sound like an idiot – we did okay but we’ve given away a couple of sloppy goals. And I think you can give away sloppy goals due to the nature of the opposition.

“It was really frustrating off the back of a good spell of results. But that is going to happen. We’ve got to understand that this league is not easy. We’ve just got to reset and pick up a few wins.”

Horsham entertain National League South rivals Torquay United in the second round of the FA Trophy this Saturday.

#1973. Liverpool transfer news: Agent confirms Andoni Iraola star in contract extension "talks" after strong Premier League start

By Lewis Nolan | 10 Nov 2026 18:21

Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson Becker is in preliminary talks over a contract extension, his agent has confirmed.

The Reds shot-stopper was the best player on the pitch on Sunday, when the Merseysiders emerged as 3-1 winners against Crystal Palace.

That Premier League victory lifted the club to fourth in the table, but Liverpool could have lost were in not for Alisson's heroics.

The Brazilian's contract will expire at the end of the season, though his agent Ze Maria has revealed that he could extend his stay at Anfield, telling WinWin: "Alisson loves Liverpool very much. We are in preliminary talks regarding a contract renewal."

Alisson has been at Liverpool since 2018, and though he is 34, fans are keen for him to remain the team's number one.

At his best, Alisson was arguably the most rounded goalkeeper in Europe, with none of his peers possessing his ability to reliably save shots, collect crosses and play out from the back.

The 34-year-old has been criticised in recent seasons for his kicking, especially after one of his passes against Arsenal on November 1 allowed the Gunners to score the only goal of the game.

However, the Brazilian made six saves and 16 recoveries against Palace, reminding supporters that he is still one of the best goalkeepers in the division.

A long-term contract should be out of the question, but the Reds should look to tie Alisson down for at least two years in order to allow teenager Lucca Brughmans to develop without the pressure of having to immediately start between the posts.

Alisson is not the only key starter set to see his contract expire at the end of the season given centre-back Virgil van Dijk will be a free agent at the end of 2026-27.

The Dutchman still wins the vast majority of his battles against opposition attackers despite now being 35, and he has shown no signs of slowing down.

Only Van Dijk, Alisson, Kostas Tsimikas and Wataru Endo are over the age of 30 in the Liverpool squad, but the latter two have never been first-team starters and are likely to leave.

Keeping the centre-back and goalkeeper beyond this season could be crucial in order to ease the transition into the Andoni Iraola era considering there are a number of younger stars in the squad such as Jeremy Jacquet and Rio Ngumoha that may benefit from their experience.

#1972. Former Rangers manager quits role after mirroring disastrous Sunderland record in 2958 day low

Former Rangers head coach Michael Beale has quit as manager of Belgian Pro League side Zulte Waregem just weeks after offering fans a refund following a heavy away defeat.

According to reports, Beale has resigned after just 177 days at the Elindus Arena, after the 4-1 defeat to Sint-Truidense saw them fall to their sixth consecutive loss, matching their worst run of results since October 7, 2018. The ex-Rangers man leaves them just four points clear of the relegation zone.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

His first managerial role since being sacked by Sunderland almost three years ago, Beale is understood to have fallen on his sword due to a breakdown in his relationship with senior figures over the club’s direction and strategy. The 46-year-old’s time started brightly as they went unbeaten in their opening five games. However, their form quickly unravelled, and they have been without a win since September 6.

"I will sit down with the board during the international break and we will put our heads together,” said Beale at the weekend. "Will I still be here when we return for our next match? A lot depends on how the discussions go. Last summer, we made a decision to concentrate on young players, but we have to accept that this group now needs help. We can't deny we are in trouble."

While the club are yet to officially confirm Beale’s departure, numerous reports say he has informed the club of his decision to depart. Bizarrely, his poor run of results means that he leaves his role with an identical record to his ill-fated spell at the Stadium of Light, where he also recorded four wins, two draws, and six losses, resulting in a 33.3% win rate after 12 games at both clubs.

Appointed by Zulte Waregem on May 19, he offered to refund fans’ ticket and travel costs following a heavy 3-0 defeat to La Louviere last month, approaching supporters at the final whistle to inform them of the reimbursement in person.

The ex-Ibrox boss first linked up with Rangers as part of the coaching staff during Steven Gerrard’s three-and-a-half-year reign in charge of the club, working as Rangers’ first-team coach as they went unbeaten to win the Scottish Premiership title in the 2020/21 season. He joined the former Liverpool icon in departing the club shortly afterwards, with the pair moving to Aston Villa in November 2021.

After leaving the Midlands upon Gerrard’s sacking shortly afterwards, Beale moved into his first managerial role with EFL Championship side Queens Park Rangers the following summer, but was poached by Rangers as a replacement for Giovanni van Bronckhorst just five months into his spell at Loftus Road, and was named the Ibrox club’s 18th permanent manager in their history in November 2022.

He was unable to replicate his previous success at Rangers though, and struggled in the main role at Ibrox. A mixed start to his tenure, saw him win record eight wins, two draws and four defeats. A 3-1 home defeat to Aberdeen sealed his fate though, with the club opting to bring an end to his time in the dugout after a third defeat in seven games. Appointed as manager of Sunderland 15 months later, his time on Wearside was a disaster, and the club parted ways with him after just nine weeks in the role, where he was succeeded by Regis Le Bris.

#1970. Brazilian Alysson becomes a starter after injury-hit first year at Villa

By Alexis Pereira | 10 Nov 2026 18:30

Alysson has taken advantage of Aston Villa’s rebuild to establish himself in unai Emery’s side, scoring in last Sunday’s 4-4 draw with Manchester United. The Brazilian winger, who joined from Gremio in January, has overcome an injury-hit first six months to become a starter in the Premier League.

Aston Villa’s season has been defined by resilience. The team lost more than half of its starters in the last transfer window, but Emery, with many signings, has reinvented his group again. They went seven games unbeaten before the current run of four without a win. Part of that change has come from a Brazilian who was already there: Alysson.

Signed in January from Gremio at the age of 19, he suffered in the first half of the year. Three different injuries kept him out of 18 games, according to Transfermarkt. As a result, he only played three games for Villa, coming off the bench against Brighton and Hove Albion and Wolverhampton Wanderers (both in February) and Chelsea (March).

‘He spent more time injured than available to train and play,’ Emery admitted last month about the player’s previous season.

With a full pre-season, the Brazilian was able to change his status and string games together. On Sunday, he scored one of the goals in the 4-4 draw with United, in a standout performance. It is an unlikely story given the right winger’s age and the pressure of the Premier League, where Gustavo Nunes, a former Gremio team-mate of Alysson, has still not made a start for Brentford, the club he has played for since August 2024.

More reliable physically, thanks to a full pre-season, the youngster was able to be available more often and take advantage of the overhaul in Villa’s attack following the departures of Morgan Rogers, Ollie Watkins and Leon Bailey. In his first months he was compared to the Jamaican winger.

‘He has more or less similar characteristics or qualities to Bailey: he is left-footed and plays on the right,’ Emery said in February. ‘And he has huge potential.’

In the first game of 2026-27, he showed he would have more time on the pitch, playing 17 minutes in the defeat to Paris Saint-Germain in the UEFA Super Cup. He then came off the bench in the next eight games, with a short break for a muscle problem in September, and his performances earned him a starting place.

Introduced at half-time in the defeat to Nottingham Forest, he arrived in the box to head in and level the score. Against Fenerbahce, he produced a good individual move on the wing, went past a defender into the area and passed for Tammy Abraham to tap in. Those displays earned him starts against Newcastle United, Viking, Manchester City, Fulham and, finally, Manchester United. Against Viking, he had a standout match for his ability to dribble and win duels, and directly caused an own goal.

At Old Trafford, he did everything but make it rain. He opened the scoring with a first-time shot through goalkeeper Senne Lammens’ legs, forced the Belgian’s rebound for Nicolas Jackson’s goal, and won the penalty converted by McGinn when he went at Diogo Dalot and was brought down. He could also have scored again, but a chip over Lammens went wide.

‘Alysson is understanding things well and is giving us what I want,’ Emery said in September.

‘Every minute he is playing, practising, he is fantastic,’ Emery added in October. ‘We can see his power. We can see that if he can get consistency, a lot of things he is doing: “Wow!”’

The numbers illustrate his role. Villa have been much more vertical this season thanks to the speed of Jackson, Johan Manzambi, George Hemmings and, of course, Alysson. The Brazilian ranks second of all players in the Premier League for sprints, with 22.7, and reached 35.4km/h in one match, the highest by a Villa player and the eighth-highest in the league, according to Sofascore. In the Champions League, despite only one start and 127 minutes across four games, he is among the leaders for successful dribbles (nine, 11th in the competition level with Jackson) and ground duels won (16).

‘Alysson was incredible,’ said Villa midfielder Emiliano Buendia after the 3-1 win over Viking. ‘He is showing all his potential and his ability to play on the wings.’

Because of his age, being in his first year in a new country and the injury history, Emery is cautious with the Brazilian. In different interviews, the Spanish manager has praised the youngster while stressing he still has a lot to learn, especially tactically.

‘He should be a player who can help us. So we need to be patient, seek consistency and be careful with him every day,’ he said on 19 October. ‘This season, he has felt some pain and we need to try to be careful, but also give him confidence so he is comfortable.’

‘Alysson is improving his consistency because he has very good individual qualities, but he also needs to understand the importance of consistency in the collective aspect: defending, attacking, positioning and understanding combinations with team-mates,’ he explained two days later.

Emery remains an admirer and sees the right winger as a possible Brazil international. ‘My expectation is that Alysson can also get there,’ he said after the call-up of Villa team-mate Joao Gomes. At 20, the forward has shown on the pitch what he can do, and if he becomes more consistent, it is only a matter of time before he is called up.

#1969. Genoa 1-2 AC Milan: Five things we learned – battery life, the marksman and the core five

AC Milan managed to get the win that they needed going into the international break, but they certainly made hard work of it.

Things were going very well at the Stadio Luigi Ferraris against an in-form Genoa side, with Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic giving Milan a two-goal lead with less than 20 minutes on the clock. Both goals came from the high press, with Ruben Amorim’s side looking full of energy.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

However, as has been the theme this year, the Rossoneri were unable to turn it into a complete performance. The second-half drop-off saw Genoa build more and more pressure, with Ellertsson’s strike from range making it a nervy finish.

Milan held on to secure a win that gets them back into the top four for now, and the search for consistency can resume after the two-week break. Oli Fisher has five things were learned from the game at the Marassi.

We are running out of words to describe this debut season for Alphadjo Cisse. If it wasn’t certain from the sample size we had already, then the Bologna games and this one today were proof that he is a right-place, right-time player.

The young Italian was perfectly positioned for Rabiot’s pull-back in the opening exchanges, as he so often is. He ghosts into scoring areas and provides the killer touch, with the goal this afternoon being perhaps his most impressive so far: a first-time finish across his body right into the corner.

The cynical side of us wants to say that Goncalo Ramos could learn a thing or two about what spots to be in inside the box, though the defence of the Portuguese is that his movement often creates these pockets of space to attack.

Cisse is one of only three players born in 2006 or later to have scored 8+ goals across all competitions in Europe’s top five leagues. The others are Lamine Yamal (13) and Paris Brunner (8). He also matched Andriy Shevchenko’s eight goals in his first 13 games for the Diavolo.

Another remarkable stat is that the 20-year-old has scored his eight goals across all competitions from just 20 shots. Some might argue that kind of hit rate is unsustainable, but it shows no signs of stopping for now.

As mentioned in the introduction, the first-half performance from Amorim’s side was something that fans can really get behind. It was intense, aggressive and front-footed. The quality wasn’t always there to turn everything into danger, but the intent was there.

In fact, it was this tenacity that yielded the two goals. The first one came after Pulisic pressed and won back possession, allowing Rabiot to square for Cisse. Then, the press again forced an error from Genoa with Ostigard’s stray pass seized by Ramos, who squared for Pulisic to net.

It serves as categorical proof that something energy levels alone can be enough to get Milan into very good positions in games. Yet, we also saw the other side of things too: when the battery runs flat, the Rossoneri can lose control of games very quickly.

As a result of this, where more polished teams might see things out comfortably or even score more goals, Milan seem to sink into a hole of self-doubt, inviting pressure through a quite obvious inability to cycle the ball and keep opponents at bay.

Injuries are partly to blame for this, because not having versatile options like Fikayo Tomori, Samuel Chukwueze, Ruben Loftus-Cheek and Alexis Saelemaekers to bring on is hurting things. The bench on paper looked very weak, and those who did come in didn’t really help the chaos.

This is what Amorim refers to when he talks about the team not being ‘ready’. For various reasons – from the treatment room being full to the team not being fully cohesive – Milan’s level fluctuates wildly both within games and from match to match.

There was a report in La Gazzetta dello Sport this morning which highlighted a rather remarkable statistic. With Luka Modric, Mario Gila and Pulisic all not in the starting line-up, Milan are yet to pick up a single point.

This is arguably the crux of the rotation issue; the idea that managing the conditions of certain players is a necessity but upsetting the spine of the team is running a big risk. We’d like to add Rabiot and Diego Moreira into the mix too, as the five players Milan cannot do without.

The Spanish centre-back, the Croatian and French midfield duo, the Belgian wing-back and the American forward are simply too important. Their presence is vital not just because of their quality and propensity to provide decisive contributions, but because they are among the select group who can actually play Amorim’s way.

Each of them had a positive performance for various reasons. Gila’s fierce competitive nature facilitates the high line, Modric is the only one skilled in ball management, Rabiot is so wise when it comes to taking up the right positions, while Moreira and Pulisic are the technical sparks.

These are the players to build around from now until the end of season, while then waiting to see what the windows bring. When any combination of those five are playing, Milan’s limitations are often brutally exposed.

MilanNews described the performance from referee Davide Massa as a ‘disaster’, and we think that is being quite generous. The experienced official never once gave the impression of having control over a game where the pace and ferocity demanded it.

There is of course the one incident that everyone is talking about: the yellow card for Marcandalli after he brought Rabiot down. From our perspective, there are absolutely no doubts about it being a sending off.

The rules for DOGSO (Denial of a Goal Scoring Opportunity) take into account distance from goal, but the Frenchman and Cisse were about to have a two-on-zero attack with the entire half to run into. There is no way Ostigard was getting back to cover, and we question why VAR did not intervene.

To make matters worse, he then dished out a yellow card to Rabiot for rightfully protesting, and gave red cards to three of the Milan coaching staff too. In general Massa’s refereeing left a lot to be desired as there was no consistency in the fouls that he was whistling, and the five yellow cards the Rossoneri got felt disproportionate to Genoa’s two.

Thankfully the Diavolo were able to get over the line and bank the win, but if things had taken a more negative turn in the second half, we would be talking about that Marcandalli incident with a lot more venom.

Koni De Winter showed up in a big way against his old club, putting in another top performance in a week where he has been linked with a move to three big Premier League clubs.

Yet, we have to question the highs and lows. To best illustrate this, here are our ratings for the Belgian from each of the last four games.

vs. Bologna: Where to begin? I think he could have done better positioning-wise on Bologna’s first, with no one else to mark in the box, and then he completely gifted the free-kick that made it 2-1 for the guests. Some good moments too, but too many mistakes tonight. Maybe a 4.5?

vs. Inter (8): He absolutely won the battle against Thuram this game and it’s not like it was an easy one either. The two had several 50-50 duels and he always came out on top. Aside from his Thuram battle, he was very good overall and deserves a high rating here.

vs. Ferencvaros (5.5): That backpass for Torriani should never be played in that way, even if Maignan is between the sticks. He admittedly got a bit unlucky with his clearance in the second half, but even then perhaps he could have done better. Anyway, for me it’s the pass which brings his rating down.

vs. Genoa (7.5): The only poor moment came inside the first 60 seconds, when he was caught out a bit by a ball over the top, but he managed to track back and at least narrow the angle. After that, he was brilliant in his positioning, showing off with some great tackles and interceptions too. Really good.

Being the central centre-back is a position that carries a lot of weight and responsibility in Amorim’s system, and what is clear is that one game De Winter can look like the perfect man for the job, and in others he looks simply unplayable (and not in the good way).

One of the reasons for these wild fluctuations could also be because the former Juventus man simply hasn’t had a break. So, it is easy to see why the management are targeting a central defender ahead of January, someone who can give everyone a breather and help keep the levels high.

#1966. Kevin De Bruyne: Premier League club ‘assessing real chances’ of signing Man City legend from Napoli

By Oliver Thomas | 10 Nov 2026 18:58, Last updated: 10 Nov 2026 19:01

One Premier League club are reportedly considering a shock move for Napoli and Belgium playmaker Kevin De Bruyne in January.

The 35-year-old spent 10 glorious years at Manchester City and earned legendary status at the Etihad Stadium where he won 19 trophies and made 422 appearances, scoring 108 goals and registering 177 assists.

City decided not to extend De Bruyne’s contract at the end of the 2024-25 season and he subsequently signed for Napoli as a free agent, embarking on a fresh challenge in Italian football.

De Bruyne’s debut campaign with Napoli was stuck by injury and he was limited to only 16 starts across all competitions, but he has since played in all 15 games across Serie A and the Champions League this term, chipping in with four goals and two assists.

The playmaker’s current contract is due to expire in June 2027, but it has been suggested that he could leave Napoli sooner than expected.

Last month, former Napoli striker Roberto Carlos Sosa stated that the “spark never really ignited” between De Bruyne and the Naples outfit.

Italian news outlet Calciomercato have since reported that De Bruyne is going through a ‘mental decline’ and the midfielder make look to pursue a sensational return to the Premier League in January.

The report adds that Everton would be interested in signing De Bruyne and have already initiated ‘first contacts’ with the player’s representatives to understand their ‘real chances’ of signing him.

In order for the transfer to materialise, Napoli would need to be convinced to sanction De Bruyne’s exit midway through the season, and it remains unknown as to whether they would demand a fee for a player with six months remaining on his contract.

De Bruyne is widely regarded as one of the best midfielders in Premier League history and thrived as an advanced playmaker at Man City behind the central striker.

He was also capable of operating as a false nine or in a deep-lying midfield role, dictating play from just in front of the back four, while he also has experience out on the right and left flanks, though he does not possess the acceleration he once had.

At Everton, De Bruyne could be a contender to play in a deeper midfield position alongside James Garner and/or Harrison Armstrong, who have featured regularly under David Moyes.

De Bruyne could also play further forward as a No.10, but this is where Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall has established himself as a key first-team figure with the Toffees.

Alternatively, the Belgian could rivals Brennan Johnson, Tyler Dibling and Merlin Rohl for starts on the right side of midfield.

The Seagulls have made an impressive start to the season and are second on 22 points after 10 matches.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Fabian Hurzeler's men are five points adrift of leaders Arsenal and one ahead of third placed Manchester City.

Brighton are also the leading scorers in the division with 26 goals and have conceded just seven times - only Arsenal have leaked fewer with five.

"There is an argument to be made that they would be the nearest pursuers to Arsenal," said Goodman, speaking to Betway.

"But I can’t see them sustaining the results that they’ll need to in order to overtake Arsenal, and the reason is Arsenal have already got a five-point cushion on Brighton.

"In terms of the rest of the teams though, they do seem to be the ones that are putting it together the best."

Brighton do have a strong squad this season but Goodman feels the demands of the Premier League and Uefa Conference League could catch up with them in the later stages.

He added: "I think winning the league might be a fraction beyond them though, and I do worry later on in the season what impact juggling European football will have on Brighton.

"When you look back to last season and you saw that Crystal Palace, Nottingham Forest and Spurs were all in a relegation battle.

"I do think that this season it looks like Sunderland for example are struggling juggling that European football with Premier League football, so it’s not uncommon.

"For Brighton to be able to sustain it through a 38-game Premier League season and a European campaign, you kind of think maybe not win the league, but absolutely, you hope that they can be challenging for a top-four Champions League spot."

Goodman, who had a prolific career as a striker for the likes of West Bromwich Albion, Sunderland and Wolves, has been impressed by the rise of Brighton and believes it’s just reward for how the club operates and long-term planning.

“I’ve been commentating for Sky Sports for 20 years next March, and I’ve commentated on Brighton and Hove Albion in League One and a lot in the Championship over that period of time,” Goodman added.

“To see the progression of the football club, along with others like Bournemouth and Brentford who are very similar in terms of the trajectory is wonderful and highlights the benefit of being a forward-thinking, well-run football club that plans ahead.

“It is wonderful to watch football clubs progress, and I think that over the last certainly few seasons since the Europa Conference League has been introduced by UEFA, it has certainly provided a happy hunting ground for Premier League clubs in terms of being able to win it.

“And there’s no reason whatsoever that Brighton cannot go on to win the Europa Conference League.

“I’m not saying it’s easy, but I’m saying with the football that they’re playing, you could make an argument that they’re the best team in it.”

#1962. Derided Thierno Barry is no longer a source of frustration as star fires Everton to victory over Coventry on another big night for David Moyes amid Jack Grealish drama

Published: 17:29 EST, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 06:27 EST, 7 November 2026

Maybe Everton should request to play under the lights every week. It certainly seems to push David Moyes' team to new heights.

Following hot on the heels of consecutive night victories over Newcastle United, Friday's 3-1 win against Coventry City was a reminder of why, under Moyes, there is renewed sense of optimism at Everton.

Up to fifth, above Liverpool, and in a Carabao Cup quarter-final at Fleetwood, it could prove to be a special season.

This always felt like a big task for Frank Lampard, back at Everton for the first time since his sacking in 2023.

Popular as the ex-manager may be, there's no room for sentiment, certainly not from Moyes on a night he took charge of his 592nd game, drawing level with Harry Catterick for managing the most games in the club's history.

He'll set it outright after the international break against Brentford and Keith Andrews, who was 21 when Moyes first took up the reins at Everton.

Thierno Barry (right) now has 10 goals this season after being widely derided in his first season on Merseyside

Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall had been left out of the England squad in the morning, but refused to let it spoil his night

His side started impressively, fashioning three shots in the opening 10 minutes, before losing all momentum and allowing Coventry into proceedings.

It took going 1-0 down, to a soft Yann Gboho goal, for the hosts to come alive. Thierno Barry, so often the source of frustration last season, was magnificent and all but won the game with a five-minute brace in the second half.

The striker didn't score his first goal until December last season. This campaign, he's reached 10 before the second international break. Moyes joked post-match that Erling Haaland should watch his back in the Golden Boot race is starting to feel less absurd. Barry now sits joint second in the charts.

Both goals against Coventry came via back post-duels. The first he confidently headed past Carl Rushworth, before bundling in a second five minutes later.

The disgruntled home fans booed the team off at half-time, yet were jubilantly cheering and signing after Barry's brace. The Frenchman danced on the pitch at full-time and was serenaded by the South Stand.

'I don't see loads of young centre-forwards scoring loads of goals in the Premier League,' said Moyes.

'He's come in and has settled in a bit more. His language and communication is better and obviously he's worked to get himself into the positions to score.'

Barry wasn't the only Everton goalscorer, of course. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall was not one of the three Everton players named in Thomas Tuchel's England squad on Friday - only Arsenal had more representatives.

EVERTON (4-2-3-1): Pickford 5; Rohl 5 (O'Brien 73min, 6), Tarkowski 5, Branthwaite 6 (Keane 89), Mykolenko 6; Armstrong 6 (Hackney 73, 6), Garner 6; Dibling 5 (Johnson 73, 5), DEWSBURY-HALL 8, George 5 (Alcaraz 90); Barry 8.

COVENTRY CITY (4-2-3-1): Rushworth 4; van Ewijk 5, Mfuni 6, Pinnock 6, Dasilva 6; Yirenkyi 6, Torp 6 (Grimes 86); Sakamoto 5 (Tchaouna 86), Rudoni 5 (Hamer 86), Gboho 6 (Thomas-Asante 73, 5); Awoniyi 5 (Cherif 87).

But the midfielder sent a pointed message to the Three Lions' boss with a superb showing that was capped with a late powerful goal to end the contest.

'It was a disappointing morning, I'm not going to lie,' Dewsbury-Hall told Sky Sports after the game. 'It's a massive dream to play for my country. I know I was close.

'Yeah, sad, but really proud of myself and how I have reacted. All I can keep doing is putting in good performances and hopefully one day I get the nod, because I'm never going to give up. I've got the mentality. I'll keep pushing and pushing and see what happens.'

'He's desperate to play for England,' added Moyes. 'You never know if England get a couple of injuries, or anything changes.'

What ended as a comfortable win could have been a different outcome had Jame Tarkowski been punished for a hair pull on Caleb Yirenkyi, or if Vitalii Mykolenko's tussle with Taiwo Awoniyi in the box had been deemed a foul.

Both were checked and cleared by VAR, as was a handball claim in the build-up to Barry's second goal.

'Tarky pulls on Caleb's hair, they [VAR] are saying it's not enough of a pull,' said an aggrieved Lampard afterwards. 'That's a hard area to be in. What is hair pull and what's not?

'I think Taiwo, on the edge of the box was a penalty. I feel there's a penalty by the time Myko's knee is in the back of Taiwo's knee on the line of the box.

'Then the Barry one is handball. He flicks it in [with the hand] with the final touch. Nothing went for us tonight.'

#1961. Man United news: INEOS and Jim Ratcliffe make Omar Berrada, Jason Wilcox 'sack' call as Michael Carrick edges towards exit

By Lewis Nolan | 10 Nov 2026 19:11

Manchester co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe still has confidence in director of football Jason Wilcox and CEO Omar Berrada, the latest report has claimed.

The future of several figures at Old Trafford have been questioned in recent weeks given the club find themselves 18th in the Premier League table.

Head coach Michael Carrick appears likely to lose his job after Wednesday, when senior leaders of Ratcliffe's INEOS group are set to meet to discuss the manager's future.

Wilcox and Berrada will reportedly be in attendance, though fans have been critical of their role in the downfall of the Red Devils and have called for their dismissal.

The Telegraph claim that both retain the support of INEOS and Ratcliffe, who has no plans to remove them from their roles.

Berrada and Wilcox were appointed in 2024, with the former having previously worked for Manchester City in a number of departments, including recruitment strategy.

Wilcox took up a role as Southampton's director of football in January 2023, and he was reportedly identified by Berrada as a key talent.

It is impossible for fans to know the true extent of their roles at Old Trafford, but the fact that United have repeatedly failed in the transfer market is a damning indictment of their time at the club.

The Red Devils focused on their attack in the summer of 2025, only for the likes of Matheus Cunha and Benjamin Sesko to disappoint, and there is still no clear left-winger in the squad other than Marcus Rashford.

United signed three midfielders in the summer of 2026, but there are serious question marks about Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos, while Carlos Baleba has struggled with injuries.

Carrick will almost certainly be relived of his coaching duties, and while results and performances suggest that it would be the right call, he has been routinely let down by those above him.

A squad's ceiling will ultimately be capped by how well the decision makers recruit in transfer markets, and the likes of Berrada and Wilcox have left the manager short in numerous areas.

Responsibility for United's struggles must ultimately fall on Ratcliffe, especially as Carrick is set to be the third boss sacked since he took control of sporting operations in 2024.

#1959. Ghana vs Somalia - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Ojele | 10 Nov 2026 20:14, Last updated: 10 Nov 2026 20:24

Ghana will be desperate to breathe life into their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign when they play host to Somalia at the Essipong Sports Stadium in the first of their Group C double-header on Thursday.

Having lost their first two matches, both nations are left with little room for mistakes and know Thursday’s result could prove decisive in shaping up their qualifying ambitions, and this makes for an exciting contest in Sekondi-Takoradi.

Two games into the race for a spot in the 2027 AFCON, Ghana find themselves amongst nine sides yet to pick up any points in the qualifiers, with the federation parting ways with Portuguese coach Carlos Queiroz and opting for a change in ideas in the dugout.

Coming off the back of a round-of-32 defeat against Colombia in the World Cup back in June, the Black Stars kicked off their AFCON qualifying campaign with a 2-0 loss against Ivory Coast on September 24, with Malick Yalcouye and Franck Kessie netting on either side of half-time to hand the Elephants all three points.

Playing in front of the home supporters five days later, Ghana failed to make home advantage count in matchday two, when they fell to a 4-2 defeat at the hands of Gambia after squandering a two-goal lead at the Accra Sports Stadium.

Ernest Nuamah and Felix Afena-Gyan hit the target to put Ghana in the driver’s seat, but strikes from Muhammed Badamosi, Omar Colley, and a second-half brace from Konyaspor striker Ebrima Colley turned the game on its head for Gambia.

The four-time African champions have now gone eight straight games without a win in the Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers, a run which saw them miss out on the 2025 AFCON, failing to feature in the continental showpiece for the first time since 2004.

Now tasked with restoring confidence and flipping the script, interim coach Kim Lars Bjorkegren faces a must-win assignment on Thursday as Ghana seek to avoid missing back-to-back AFCON tournaments for the first time since their three successive absences in 1986, 1988 and 1990.

Like the home side, Somalia journey to the Essipong Sports Stadium with the same urgent need for a result if they are to turn their fortunes around and secure a first-ever qualification for the Africa Cup of Nations.

Having edged out Eswatini and Mauritius in the preliminary phase, the Ocean Stars fell to a 2-1 loss against Gambia in the Group C opener on September 25, with Ebrima Colley and Muhammed Badamosi netting on either side of Bilal Njie’s 72nd-minute equaliser to hand the hosts all three points at the Independence Stadium.

While there were positives to take from the defeat against Gambia, Somalia were left spitting feathers four days later, when they fell to a 2-0 defeat against Ivory Coast through strikes from Yann Gboho and Bazoumana Toure in the final six minutes at the Stade Felix Houphouet-Boigny.

Yusuf Ali’s men demonstrated their ability to rise to the occasion against quality opposition last time out when they pushed Ivory Coast to the limit, and they will have reason to believe they can upset the odds against a Ghana side currently far from convincing.

Ghana Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Somalia Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Newly-appointed Ghana boss Bjorkegren has called up 26 players to the squad for October’s double-header with Somalia, including the Premier League trio of Abdul Fatawu Issahaku, Brandon Thomas-Asante and Ibrahim Osman.

Having missed the first two qualifying matches through a groin problem, Jordan Ayew has been recalled to the squad, and the nation’s captain will hope his leadership and wealth of experience can count for something.

The Black Stars will also be lifted by the return of Tottenham Hotspur forward Mohammed Kudus, who is set to make his first international appearance of the year after missing the World Cup through an injury.

Manchester City forward Antoine Semenyo misses out through a knee injury, while 31-year-old defender Jan Gyamerah, who made his debut against Mexico on May 26, is also ruled out through a muscle problem.

Before their late collapse, Somalia held their own against a superior and more experienced Ivory Coast side last time out, and we expect Ali to name a similar XI on Thursday, with Mohamed Mohamed, Abel Gigli, Ali Omar and Faisal Othman shielding 20-year-old Ibrahim Ahmed Hussein between the sticks.

With eight goal involvements in his last nine matches for club and country, KFUM Oslo striker Nije is currently in fine form, and the 28-year-old striker should lead the Ocean Stars attack once again, while Mohamed Omar, Abdi Sharif and Mukhtar Suleiman should team up in midfield.

Ati-Zigi; Seidu, Adjetey, Salisu, Mensah; Partey, Yirenkyi; Kudus, Abdul Fatawu, Ayew; Thomas-Asante

Hussein; Mohamed, Gigli, A. Omar, Osman; M. Omar, Sharif, Suleiman; Addo, Njie, Hassan

Despite the quality in their rank, Ghana have failed an impression in the AFCON qualifiers so far, but victory on Thursday could provide the spark needed to turn their Group C campaign around.

Although Somalia have shown glimpses of their potential in their opening two matches, the difference in individual quality could prove a decisive factor here, with Ghana tipped to come away with all three points in front of their home supporters.

#1956. GdS: Fluidity, gifts and a tense finale – how Milan overcame Genoa to reclaim top four spot

AC Milan won away from home against an in-form Genoa side to ensure they will go into the international break inside the top four.

La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) have analysed a second consecutive Serie A victory for Milan, remarking that if it were it not for the nuisance of the Europa League – specifically that ugly defeat to Ferencváros – they would be heading into the break in perfect spirits.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Still, things have worked out well enough: the win at Marassi, combined with Como’s loss against Inter, has allowed Rúben Amorim’s side to leapfrog Cesc Fàbregas’s team and move into fourth place. It is of course the final spot for Champions League qualification, the minimum objective.

The question remains the same: which is the ‘real’ Milan? The one that put two goals past Genoa in the opening 20 minutes, or the one that nearly threw it all away with a passive final 20 minutes of the game?

Daniele De Rossi almost snatched a point thanks to his substitutions, while Amorim nearly dropped two points due to his own, less-than-effective changes. It seems clear that there is an issue with the squad’s overall competitiveness, with help needed in January.

In Genoa, Amorim opted for a 4-4-2 formation to start, with Yunus Musah deployed as a surprise left-back and a central midfield pairing of Luka Modrić and Adrien Rabiot.

Just seconds after kick-off, Genoa nearly took a 1-0 lead through Osmajic, who surged deep into the final third. Shaken into life by this, Milan took control and built a 2-0 lead.

In the second half, the team gradually shifted into a classic 3-5-2, eventually dropping into a five-man defensive line to hold firm after Ellertsson’s goal. In modern football, fluidity is an asset though it carries the risk of lacking a clear, defined identity.

Milan dominated for long stretches of the first half, particularly on the flanks, but found themselves under significant duress toward the end of the match. The data on the average position of the team is telling: Genoa finished at 55.6 metres, while Milan sat at 44.3.

Anyone unaware of the final score when looking at the stats might well imagine a different outcome, while it remains unclear if the team dropping so deep was instruction or protective instinct. However, the Diavolo survived.

The reality is that sometimes errors – individual or otherwise – have a greater impact on results than good intentions or tactical formations. Genoa arrived at this match on the back of three consecutive victories, though they were missing Frendrup, the Dane who acts as the team’s stabiliser.

Having already enjoyed a string of successes, the team grew complacent. It was a feeling only intensified by the golden opportunity that fell to Osmajic in the opening minutes. Genoa lulled themselves into a false sense of security, and some players began to switch off.

There was an early warning sign when Vasquez gifted the ball to Gonçalo Ramos, though the Portuguese forward’s shot went wide. Later, Vasquez was dispossessed again – this time by Pulisic – sparking the sequence that led to the 0-1 goal: a touch to Rabiot, a cross for Cissé and a finish.

Milan then shifted their focus to the left flank. Under pressure from Cissé, Traoré played a disastrous pass toward Østigård inside the box. The Norwegian failed to clear it, and Ramos set up Pulisic just inside the area for the goal that made it 0-2.

At 2-0, the game opened up for Milan, who favoured direct, vertical play over patient possession. The attacking combinations on the flanks proved decisive: Moreira operated on one side, working alongside Pulisic, who was given the freedom to roam between the penalty area, the final third, and the wing.

The duo of Musah and Cissé dominated their flank against Marcandalli and Ehizibue. Deploying Musah as a left-back was a tactical move De Rossi likely hadn’t anticipated. Was it all over? Had the match been decided? Not quite. Before the half-time whistle, Genoa showed signs of a resurgence.

In the second half, the atmosphere turned hostile, and referee Massa had to send four people off from the benches to restore some semblance of order. Then, a flurry of substitutions narrowed the gap between Genoa and Milan.

When El Shaarawy came on, De Rossi found more space to push forward. When Pulisic was taken off, Amorim’s side lost ground. Ellertsson’s goal – a beautiful strike, aided by a lack of marking from Jashari – set the stall out for a frantic final stretch, during which Milan risked conceding an equaliser.

if you tally up the chances and shots on target, the scales actually tip in favor of the Grifone. So, what does this mean? Is all well that ends well? Is a Champions League spot guaranteed? Certainly not. The impression is that this Milan is still in a phase where anything is possible, in either direction.

A return to the Champions League is far from certain, but the table is tight. League-leaders Lazio are only five points ahead, less than two wins away, so who’s to say Milan can’t aim higher?

Much will depend on January. The winter window shouldn’t be about patching things up, as quick fixes often end up being worse than the original problems. Rather, Gerry Cardinale (plus potentially Markus Krösche) should think about genuine improvement.

It will also depend on Amorim and his ability to shape the squad, ironing out the deficiencies. In the background, the question of Gonçalo Ramos remains. He showed commendable selflessness at Marassi, but he needs to start scoring himself soon.

For now, Cissé is stepping up, having netted his eighth goal of the season and his fifth in Serie A. Roberto Mancini is now waiting for him with the senior national team, which is just the latest step in a fairytale start to 2026-27.

#1951. Cucurella defends Vinicius Jr over Diomande comparison as Real Madrid pause eight-game winning run

By Alexis Pereira | 10 Nov 2026 20:52

Marc Cucurella has defended Vinicius Junior amid the Brazilian’s difficult start to the season, insisting that team-mate Yan Diomande does not help him more defensively than the Real Madrid forward does. Real Madrid have paused an eight-game winning run for the international break, during the best spell under boss Jose Mourinho, and are hoping Vinicius rediscovers his form with Brazil under Carlo Ancelotti. Cucurella shares that wish.

Speaking on the Cope radio programme El Partidazo, the Spanish left-back was asked about the poor start to the season of Vinicius, who has just one goal and three assists in 12 matches. The decline in his form, together with a suspension that kept him out of the last four La Liga games, has led to the meteoric rise of Diomande, who has made a difference on the left side.

Beyond four goals and four assists in 16 matches, the Ivory Coast forward has been praised for his tactical commitment, helping Cucurella with defensive recovery. But the Real Madrid number 17 rejects the idea that Diomande helps him more with marking than the Brazilian does.

‘I do not think he helps me more, I think he is more visible,’ Cucurella said. ‘Diomande runs back and is everywhere. Vinicius goes back three times and then, the fourth time he does not run, the ball is played in. If Vini scored three goals per game, nobody would say anything to him.’

Days after his signing from Chelsea was announced in late June, the defender told Radio Marca that he ‘did not mind’ if Vinicius ‘does not track back or help in defence’, because he wanted the number seven energised to have an impact in the final third with goals. Cucurella also told Vinicius that he would do all the ‘dirty work’ for him.

Despite that consent, the forward has helped with the compactness without the ball, following the Portuguese boss’s guidance. The main problem is that, in possession, the 26-year-old has not shown the same efficiency as in recent years in dribbles in one-on-one situations and in decision-making.

Like other figures at Real Madrid, the Spaniard came out in defence of Vinicius, considering a dip in form natural after consecutive seasons among the best players in the world. The left-back also insisted that Vinicius has been working behind the scenes to react and regain his prominence, which he considers fundamental to Mourinho’s success in 2026-27.

‘Vinicius is a player who has been performing at a spectacular level for five years, so it is understandable that he is going through a difficult phase now,’ Cucurella continued. ‘I see that he is motivated and works hard in training, and that is what matters.’

‘The most important thing for us is that he returns to his best level, because if he is at his peak, we have a great team,’ he concluded.

#1948. 'People keep telling me it's great I'm managing against my son... it's not - it's horrible': Peterborough boss ROBBIE SAVAGE and Reading star CHARLIE on their 'awkward' FA Cup showdown, playing for Man United and dangers facing modern young players

Published: 02:00 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 09:02 EST, 7 November 2026

The FA Cup cast its spell upon the Savages while they were out shopping for groceries.

Reading midfielder Charlie was strolling the aisles of the Marks & Spencer foodhall with his girlfriend when his phone began to buzz. He remembered it was first-round draw day.

He fished out the phone, saw the cascade of messages and realised, as they like to say in M&S, this was not just any FA Cup draw. He called his dad.

Peterborough United boss Robbie was in the Co-op. He had stopped on his way back to the rented lodgings he describes as a 'little annexe in someone's garden' and was rummaging through the ready meals in search of a spaghetti bolognese for one when he answered.

'The reception in Peterborough isn't great, it kept cutting out,' Robbie tells Daily Mail Sport. 'Charlie said: "You won't believe the draw." I thought he was going to say Forest Green. Or Macclesfield. I didn't think about Reading. He said: "You've got us." I just went: "Oh no."'

They were on a collision course from the moment Robbie left Forest Green for the Posh job last month. The teams were scheduled to meet in League One next month at Reading but the FA Cup draw caught them off guard.

Peterborough boss Robbie Savage (right) with his son, Reading midfielder Charlie. The pair will meet in the FA Cup first round at London Road on Saturday

'This will be the first time I hope my son doesn't have an impact, which is a horrible feeling,' Robbie tells Daily Mail Sport

And while they were both at great pains to stress that Saturday's tie at London Road, screened live on TNT Sports, is about Peterborough and Reading not their little family gathering, they can appreciate the fuss.

'Football is a beautiful game, it brings people together and creates rivalries,' says Charlie. 'This week it's created a rivalry in our family. I'm not sure who my mum, brother, grandparents and cousins will support but there's no better time for them to have a half-and-half scarf.'

For Robbie, the beauty of the occasion is yet to unfurl itself. 'It's going to be horrible,' he says. 'Every time I watch my sons play, I'm anxious. I'm nervous. I want them to do well. If they give the ball away and the other team attack, I've got butterflies thinking, "Please don't score".

'This will be the first time I hope my son doesn't have an impact, which is a horrible feeling. People keep telling me it's great. I've got to say it's not great, it's horrible. Usually we speak every day and I've not been able to speak to him all week because I don't want to put him in a position where anything gets out and anyone can point a finger at him.

'I don't want it to be billed as Savage v Savage because it's not. Charlie might not play but if he plays and makes a mistake and we score the winner, so be it. If he plays and scores the winner, well, wow.'

Robbie puffs out his cheeks and widens his eyes as he considers this scenario. 'We've got to win for Peterborough United,' he adds.

Ironically, it was a passion relit by coaching his sons which tempted the former Leicester, Birmingham and Blackburn midfielder out of the comfort of his media work and into coaching. Savage helped out with his youngest son Freddie's Under 13s team in the Timperley and District Junior Sunday League.

'Standing out at training on a Tuesday and Thursday night,' says Robbie. 'Sunday morning, putting the nets up. I've been that dad. In the first season we were hammered 13-0, but we built a team and won a lot of things.'

Charlie Savage in action for Reading. The midfielder played 45 games for the club last season but has yet to start a league match during this campaign

Savage offers some advice to his team in his new role as manager of Peterborough

Two years ago, Charlie and Freddie implored their father to follow his heart and make the switch from sporting director to manager at Macclesfield in the Northern Premier League.

'Even back then, he said one day he'd manage against me,' Charlie tells Daily Mail Sport. 'I was in League One and he was in Step Three and I'm thinking, "Well, give it a few years", but he always gets where he wants to get to.

'He's a competitor. He wants to win, wants to succeed. Even with my little brother's team it hurt him to lose in Sunday morning grassroots football. That's something inside him and it won't change.

'He will want to beat us. Unfortunately for him, I'm the same. I want to win. There might be an awkward car journey home.'

Charlie's memories of his father playing football are from Derby, the last stop of a 15-year professional career which started at Manchester United and took in seven different clubs, as well as 39 Wales caps. 'I remember seeing his long hair, scurrying around the pitch,' says the 23-year-old. 'Throwing his arms up and shouting at the refs.'

Like his dad, Charlie also came through United's youth ranks and made one first-team appearance, as a substitute at the age of 18 against Young Boys in the Champions League. It was an unforgettable night for Robbie, who was on co-commentary duty with a lump in his throat.

'He'll always have that on me,' says Robbie. 'All I ever wanted to do from 14 to 19 was play for one minute in Manchester United's first team. It didn't happen and he's done it. His name is on the wall at Carrington and mine isn't.

'I'm so glad his name is there instead of mine. You want the best for your sons. I'm proud of both my sons.'

Charlie has three Wales caps and counting. His father won 39...

...but despite both Charlie and Robbie coming through the Manchester United academy, only Charlie played for the first team (above), against Young Boys at Old Trafford in 2021

Freddie is studying for an economics degree at the University of Manchester. Charlie left United for Reading four years ago and now has 175 senior appearances and three Wales caps under his belt and a reputation in his own right.

'He's got a great left foot, passing range and incredible running ability,' says Robbie. 'He's intelligent. Nine As in his GCSEs. He doesn't drink, he lives his life 24 hours a day, seven days a week to be a footballer. He's a down-to-earth, humble kid.

'He was so brave to go and play senior football when he had three years left at Manchester United, and it's paid off. He played 45 games last season. He hasn't started a league game this season but hasn't sulked.

'I was a sulker, as Martin O'Neill and Nigel Clough (who coached Savage at Leicester and Derby respectively) will tell you. If that was me, my body language would be negative, but he's got a great attitude. And I've tried to tell him now he has to train harder than ever and conduct himself in the right way.'

If Robbie is a guiding light and inspiration for Charlie, vital information flows both ways for an aspiring manager with a young team.

'The mindset of a Millennial is completely different to when I played,' says the 52-year-old Posh boss. 'If they're not in the team or the manager has shouted at them, they go home to an apartment where they live alone away from their families, isolated from 2pm to 7am with all that time to think about it.

'We have to understand their vulnerabilities on and off the pitch. Charlie has been through that so without knowing it, he's made me a better manager. I try to think about what's best for my players, what I'd want a manager to do for Charlie in that situation.'

'He gives it out and he can take it and, unfortunately, it has become part of his life to be on the receiving end,' Charlie says of his dad Robbie

'Great left foot, passing range and incredible running ability,' says Robbie of his son Charlie

Being the Son of Sav cannot be easy. Not only the added scrutiny and expectation, and accusations doors have been opened for him by a famous and influential father, but also in a world where footballers are too often considered fair game for abuse whether inside the stadium or online.

'It's there in all forms of life,' admits Charlie. 'Maybe people subconsciously want me to fail a little bit more because of who he is. I get it. Football is a game and my dad is a divisive figure inside that game.

'He gives it out and he can take it and, unfortunately, it has become part of his life to be on the receiving end. Sometimes the abuse goes too far. People forget he's a human not just a football personality.

'But I wouldn't change who he is. I wouldn't change having him as my dad, I'm very proud of him.'

#1945. Barcelona Women vs Arsenal Women - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ben Sully | 10 Nov 2026 21:06, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 10:27

Arsenal Women will travel to Camp Nou for Thursday's highly anticipated meeting with reigning European Champions Barcelona Women.

The Gunners are sitting in fifth spot in the Women's Champions League league phase, while the Catalan giants are flying high at the top of the standings with a perfect record.

Barcelona have made the perfect start to their bid to win a fifth UWCL title, having won their opening three league phase games by a combined 19-2 scoreline.

After comfortably dispatching Paris FC and Roma, Barcelona made light work of their clash against Koge on matchday three, with Claudia Pina netting a brace in an emphatic 8-0 victory in Denmark.

Barcelona returned to Liga F action with a 4-0 success against fellow Catalan side Badalona, before they eased to a 5-1 victory in Sunday's meeting with Madrid CFF, moving them four points clear of second-placed Real Madrid at the top of the standings.

Those two league wins have helped Barcelona build a four-game winning run since suffering a surprise 2-1 away loss against Real Sociedad on October 18.

While they experienced a blip on their travels, Barcelona have won all six of their competitive home games this season, scoring at least five goals in five of those victories.

The Blaugrana have also won 33 of their 35 UWCL home games (D1, L1), including each of their last 11 European home assignments since losing 1-0 to Chelsea in the first leg of their semi-final tie in April 2024.

Arsenal, meanwhile, have struggled for consistency in domestic action this season, with Renee Slegers's side sitting in sixth spot and six points adrift of the top three after recording three wins, four draws and two defeats in nine Women's Super League games.

Having taken seven points from their three European games, the Gunners are at least in a better position in the Women's Champions League, even if their first two performances were far from convincing.

Arsenal required a 93rd-minute penalty to see off Koge on matchday one, before they spurned a goal lead in a frustrating 2-2 draw against Paris FC in the French capital.

The Gunners at least made light work of their home game against Benfica, which saw Alessia Russo net a hat-trick in a commanding 3-0 victory at Meadow Park to become the leading English scorer in UWCL history with 23 goals.

Russo went on to score in a 1-1 draw against Aston Villa before registering a brace in Sunday's 2-1 away win over Liverpool, meaning she has now scored nine goals in Arsenal's last seven competitive matches.

The in-form forward will be hoping to continue her impressive form in Thursday's fixture, as Arsenal look for a repeat of the memorable 1-0 victory they recorded in their most recent meeting with Barcelona in the 2024-25 UWCL final in Lisbon.

Green said of the win at EG: “I thought we thoroughly deserved the win.

“Defensively we were very, very good. We have a few injuries so had to play Harry Shooman at centre-half with Henry Watson and the pair were immense.

“The game was cagey in spells and opened up in spells, it was a proper game of football but I felt we were the better side.

“We were pleased to get the three points and it was nice to get the win over a team who are up there competing with us – a good day at the office.”

Heath have won five SCFL games in a row but Green said: “We’re not looking beyond each game as it comes.

“The league is a tough one this year and we know most teams can beat each other so it’s about not looking too far ahead and just looking at the next game and making sure we’re the best version of ourselves.”

Heath host AFC Varndeanians on Saturday, then Broadbridge Heath in the Sussex Senior Cup on Tuesday.

That is one of three cups they’re still in – they’ve had good recent wins over Hailsham in the RUR, and Worthing United, where they won 7-1, in the Peter Bentley.

Green said: “We were very good at Worthing United against a team who have been going very well this season. They were pretty good first half but we went up a level second half and took the game away from them so that was pleasing.

“Broadbridge Heath will be interesting. They’re going well a division above us so we’re looking forward to that. Hopefully we can get a big crowd in.”

Injury problems continue, Green saying: “On Saturday we were missing Nathan Stroomberg, Jack Barnes, Sam Remfry and Joe Allman. Charlie Towning broke his wrist in the FA Vase game at Rusthall.”

#1943. Dele Alli risks the wrath of Spurs fans as he wears an ARSENAL shirt on livestream - with ex-Tottenham star livid after losing bet to influencer iShowSpeed

By BEN WILLCOCKS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 09:49 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 09:53 EST, 7 November 2026

Dele Alli has risked infuriating Tottenham supporters after wearing an Arsenal jersey on a Twitch livestream.

The former England midfielder, whose once-bright career has been in freefall since his exit from Tottenham in 2022, has been keeping himself busy on a series of livestreams with fans as he continues to look for a new club.

The 30-year-old star, who has been a free agent since leaving Como in September 2025, joined iShowSpeed on stream after the American influencer challenged him to a game of EAFC 27.

Dele, who played as Saudi Arabian outfit Al-Qadsiah, was beaten 4-2 by iShowSpeed's Al-Nassr and reacted so angrily to missing a late chance that he furiously smashed his controller.

Egged on by the influencer saying, "I ain't gonna lie, throw the controller, break it", as he missed an open goal, the footballer left his chair and started repeatedly launching it against the floor.

Dele's punishment for losing the bet was to wear an Arsenal shirt live on stream, and the former Tottenham midfielder reluctantly obliged.

Dele Alli has risked infuriating Spurs fans after wearing an Arsenal jersey (@dele/instagram)

The ex-Spurs star once said he would rather retire than play for north London rivals Arsenal

Dele Alli looks good in an Arsenal kit, he must be feeling victorious 😂😂 pic.twitter.com/62cO7iYm2w

Sporting the jersey of his old team's bitter north London rivals, which had been delivered to his home by a friend, Dele burrowed his head in his hands with discomfort as fans caught a glimpse of him representing Arsenal for the first time.

Gunners supporters were greatly amused as videos and images of Dele, who in 2016 said he would rather retire than play for Arsenal, went viral on social media.

'Dele Alli looks good in an Arsenal kit, he must be feeling victorious,' one fan posted to X with a string of laughing emojis.

He later posted a selfie to his Instagram, saying: 'Sorry Spurs fans but a bet is a bet. Congrats iShowSpeed.'

Although a regular streamer nowadays, Dele was once lauded as one of English football's greatest talents, having burst on to the scene under Mauricio Pochettino and carving out almost 200 appearances for the north London club.

He is now making a habit of phoning old team-mates for a chat in front of his audience of followers on stream, having held brief conversations with both Jack Grealish and Tottenham legend Harry Kane.
